node.name: Introduction to R: A Hands-on Workshop (Part 1)
node.descriptionText:
Registration needed. In Person event

Overview:
Have data you'd like to analyze but don't know where to start with R? This beginner-friendly, two-part workshop takes you from opening R for the first time to producing a clean dataset, summary tables and publication-ready plots.

We'll work with a realistic (fictional) measles outbreak dataset that has the kinds of problems real data has: messy column names, impossible values, inconsistent categories and dates stored as text. You'll code along with the instructor and practice each skill right away in short exercises, with helpers in the room to get you unstuck. Clinical, public health and laboratory researchers are all welcome.

Part 1 (Nov 20): From raw file to clean data
By the end of Part 1, you will be able to:

Set up an R project in Positron so your code and data stay organized and easy to find
Use R's building blocks: objects, vectors, functions and missing values (NA), and find help when you're stuck
Import data from CSV and Excel files
Inspect a dataset to spot problems such as wrong data types, impossible values, typos and missing data
Clean data with the tidyverse: tidy column names, fix dates, recode categories and create new variables like age groups
Save your clean dataset so you can pick up where you left off
Part 2 (Dec 4): From clean data to results
By the end of Part 2, you will be able to:

Handle missing values and duplicate records
Combine datasets with joins, for example adding population sizes to calculate case rates
Summarize data with counts, percentages and group-wise statistics
Visualize data with ggplot2: build histograms, box plots and bar charts, label them clearly, and save them
Create a "Table 1" of participant characteristics with gtsummary and export it to Word
Leave with a complete, reusable R script you can adapt to your own data
Who should attend
Beginners with no prior programming experience. If you've used Excel, you're ready. We recommend attending both parts. If you already know basic R (importing data, mutate(), the pipe), you're welcome to join Part 2 only; a ready-made clean dataset will be provided.

Before the workshop
Please bring a laptop and install R, Positron and the workshop packages before Part 1, using the setup instructions. Setup takes about 30 minutes and ends with a short test, so you'll know you're ready. Bring the same laptop and workshop folder to Part 2. If you get stuck, contact maximilian.wegener@yale.edu or sofia.fertuzinhos@yale.edu before the workshop.

node.name: Daily Worship and Communion at Marquand Chapel
node.descriptionText:
Join us at 11:30am in Marquand Chapel for our daily worship.

Worship in Marquand often draws on a wide variety of inherited Christian traditions, with the worship of many denominations being represented. Beyond that, though, we also pay attention to the rising number of people in Western society who have a lively interest in spirituality but feel no connection to traditional forms of church and worship. So Marquand is also actively engaged in original, creative, and experimental forms of worship, both for committed Christians and for those exploring the faith.

node.name: Women in AI Collective: Build A Bot Workshop
node.descriptionText:
Build a Bot is a hands-on workshop for participants to design and create a functional AI chatbot using generative AI tools available at Yale. Attendees will learn the fundamentals of bot design — from defining a use case and structuring instructions, to testing and refining outputs — and leave with a working bot tailored to their own research, teaching, or administrative needs. Whether the goal is to streamline a recurring task, support a course, or assist with day-to-day administrative work, this session walks through the process step by step: identifying a clear purpose, drafting effective instructions, and iterating based on real responses. No coding experience is necessary. Participants should leave the session with both a working prototype and a repeatable process they can apply to future bot-building projects.

Attendees are also required to bring a laptop to this workshop.

Attendance will be capped at 50 people.

node.name: AI for Research and Writing Series Part 3
node.descriptionText:
Using artificial intelligence for research and writing has emerged as a helpful skillset in any scholar’s toolkit. AI tools can find sources, read and summarize articles, write text and code, manage workflows, and identify impactful research questions. In this workshop series, participants will reflect on their own research to identify opportunities for AI to boost their productivity and impact. Through hands-on practice with AI tools adopted by Yale, participants will explore how AI can advance their projects at each stage of the writing process. Join us for:

Intro to AI for Literature Reviews and Reading (11/6)
Intro to AI for Writing (11/13)
Workflow Management with AI (11/20)

Intended audience: Graduate students in all disciplines.

node.name: Men’s Giving: Celebrating Our Men Together
node.descriptionText:
Presented by the Yale Black Culture Network's Men's Collective in Partnership with Vaughn Signatures

In recognition of Movember and Men's Mental Health Awareness, the Yale Black Culture Network's Men's Collective, in partnership with Vaughn Signatures, invites you to our inaugural Men's Giving, a meaningful gathering dedicated to reflection, connection, personal growth, and the power of community.

This event creates an intentional space for men to reflect on who we are, the challenges we navigate, and the strength found in vulnerability, shared experiences, and supporting one another. Through guided small-group dialogues that honor every voice, we will explore men's mental health, identity, purpose, and the importance of building meaningful connections that extend beyond the event.

What to Expect:
- Guided conversations that encourage reflection, learning, and growth
- Small-group dialogues rooted in authenticity, respect, and understanding

- Opportunities to build community and meaningful connections
- Access to resources supporting men's mental health and well-being
- Complimentary food and fellowship

node.descriptionText:
November 21, 2026 | 7:30pm | Commons

Instructions

Commons is located at Yale Schwarzman Center, 168 Grove Street, New Haven, CT 06511.

This event is free and open to the public.
If you need technical assistance with registration or require accessible accommodations contact ysc.info@yale.edu.

One of the most celebrated Odissi performers, teachers, choreographers, and scholars of her generation, Bijayini Satpathy spent nearly three decades as a principal dancer and Director of Training and Outreach at Nrityagram, one of India’s foremost dance institutions. Her artistic work has been recognized globally through prestigious appointments including Artist-in-Residence at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, and Fellow at the Center for Ballet and the Arts, New York University. She also served as the Alma Hawkins Visiting Chair at UCLA’s Department of World Arts and Cultures/Dance. 

Her performances are precise, deeply spiritual, and achingly beautiful — rooted in a classical tradition that is thousands of years old and somehow completely alive in her hands.

node.name: University Church in Yale Worship
node.descriptionText:
The University Church in Yale is a student-focused church welcoming Christian students of all backgrounds, as well as staff, faculty, post-docs, parents, alumnus/a, parents, and our New Haven neighbors.

Our church life is centered around Sunday worship in Yale’s historic Battell Chapel, which features beautiful music, thoughtful preaching, and the prayer of a diverse, faithful community. Outside of Sunday mornings, we have lots of fun together with retreats, study groups, meals, concerts, lectures and other events.

UCY is an open and affirming congregation; we welcome persons of any denominational background (or none), race, ethnicity, age, nationality, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, or physical or mental ability. Whether you are a life-long Christian, a questioning Christian, or new to Christianity, we hope that you feel at home with us.
